subject.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations

question: Should OpenClaw allow `constructor` and `prototype` as direct `browser.profiles` keys while keeping them blocked at every nested config path, and accept Browser trash authority limited to `CONFIG_DIR/browser`?
rationale: The code path is narrow and tested, but it changes a shared prototype-pollution guard and filesystem-trash authority boundary, which automation should not own as a permanent security decision.

options.title: Accept Scoped Boundary
options.body: Allow only direct `browser.profiles.constructor` and `browser.profiles.prototype` records, keep nested blocked keys filtered, and proceed after exact-head merge gates remain green.

options.title: Reserve Blocked Names
options.body: Reject `constructor` and `prototype` in Browser profile validation/schema and keep the shared merge-patch guard strict everywhere.

options.title: Pause For Encoded Keys
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want profile IDs encoded so blocked object names never appear directly in config patches.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Boundary
recommendation.body: Allow only direct `browser.profiles.constructor` and `browser.profiles.prototype` records, keep nested blocked keys filtered, and proceed after exact-head merge gates remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned and has the strongest recent Browser/config/security-boundary history for this surface.
